name: ChronoLLM
own_description: Competitive training of chronologically consistent Large Language Models

paragraphs: A ChronoLLM miner trains a language model for each year from 2013 through 2024, using only information available by that year’s cutoff. Miners upload the models to Hugging Face and submit a public list linking each year to an exact model commit. They submit it with a registered subnet 38 hotkey, which is the key a miner works with.

Training requires a GPU, and automatic upload requires a Hugging Face write token. The guide specifies no minimum GPU memory, disk space, public port, always-on miner server, extra fee or post-registration protection period. The optional CPU self-test allows 12 calls per hotkey daily.

Validators, who are participants who score the miners’ work, test knowledge from before and after each cutoff and then compare qualifying models’ completions head to head. The README describes ranking by wins alone, but the code defaults to 30% for the cutoff test and 70% for the duel win rate. Up to ten miners share the miner allocation by rank, and when ten earn rewards, the first three receive about 52%, 23% and 12% of that allocation.

Each weekly submission is due Monday at 12:00 UTC, and private models must be public before 13:00 UTC that day. Any year you miss scores zero. Read from https://github.com/chronollm/sn38 at commit 1c093d4 on 2026-11-23.
mining_note.how_it_was_made: This note was put together by AI agents and not by a person who mines here. One agent read the subnet's public repository and wrote down what a miner does, what it takes and how the work is paid, with a source for each statement, and a second agent opened every source and took out whatever it did not support. Of 20 source checks, 19 held, 0 did not hold and 1 could not be opened, and only what held is in the text above. Nothing of the subnet's code was run, and the note describes the code as it stood on the day and at the commit named in its last sentence, so it can be out of date.
